title: Stream-bound kernel sequencing and span transactionization
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: Current runtime telemetry emits many NVTX ranges and kernel-level spans, but we lack a stable way to stitch per-kernel events into higher-level 'transactions' that represent a single request's prefill or decode lifecycle. This makes it hard to answer: which kernel choices and attention pathways contributed to tail latency on a per-request basis, and how does kernel variability correlate with sequence length/batch composition. Goal: implement "transactionization" - a deterministic mapping from low-level NVTX/span events into hierarchical request-level transactions with stable fingerprints. Deliver an end-to-end pipeline: (1) instrumentation changes in the runtime to emit a small set of affinity tags and an exec_ctx_hash for each kernel invocation; (2) a lightweight client-side coalescer that groups spans into transactions before export; (3) updates to our metrics exporter to populate per-transaction counters and per-kernel histograms keyed by seq_len_bucket, batch_size, kernel_variant, and exec_ctx_hash. The feature should be low-overhead in the hot path (<1% P50 latency regression) and opt-out via a config flag. This ticket covers design, runtime changes, exporter changes, integration tests, and a dashboard prototype.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits kernel events with stable exec_ctx_hash and affinity tags for every prefill/decode kernel invocation.
Backend coalescer groups spans into transactions with >99% precision on synthetic tests and explains remaining mismatches.
Per-transaction metrics exported: total_token_time_ms, kernel_count, peak_kernel_latency_ms, exec_ctx_entropy_score, sequence_length_bucket, and kernel_variant_breakdown.
End-to-end overhead measured and verified: P50 regression <1%, P99 regression <3% on a production-like workload using a small canary.
Dashboard with drill-down: select exec_ctx_hash -> show associated kernel timeline, per-kernel histograms, and attention-path annotations.
Docs updated: instrumentation notes, opt-out config, and migration guide for existing dashboards.
technical_notes: Instrumentation: add two small tags on kernel entry: affinity_tag (stream_slot:<int>|phase:prefill|decode) and exec_ctx_hash (64-bit hex). Do not allocate heap on hot path; compute exec_ctx_hash via xor-fold of request id + route fingerprint + sequence-length bucket.
Span boundaries: emit NVTX ranges as now but attach mini-metadata via existing span attributes (no extra allocations) so exporters can correlate without full-tracing dependence.
Coalescer: implement in exporter as a sliding-window grouping keyed by exec_ctx_hash + start_time bucket. Keep memory bounded by evicting after 2s of inactivity per transaction.
Metrics: per-kernel histograms should include labels: kernel_name, variant (quantized/float), seq_len_bucket (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512), batch_size, affinity_tag.
Exec_ctx_entropy_score: a lightweight metric computed from variance of per-kernel latencies within the transaction; used for regression alerts.
Backwards compatibility: fall back to current span-only flow if exec_ctx_hash absent; mark those transactions with "legacy_flow" label.
Testing: synthetic harness that emits adversarial interleaving across multiple streams to validate grouping boundary correctness and false-positive rate.
Security/PII: exec_ctx_hash should be non-reversible and not include user-identifiable data. Use salt from config.
